criteria.criterion: UC-AddTodo Error Case E_STORE_WRITE_FAILED - stderr message + exit 1, never a bare stack trace (ux-behavior Global convention)
criteria.evidence: repo.save() is not wrapped in try/catch at bin/todo.js:27 (cmdDone bin/todo.js:73 and cmdRm bin/todo.js:105 both are). Probe: HOME=/tmp/rp1b with chmod 444 store + chmod 555 dir, `node bin/todo.js add second` -> exit 1 with an uncaught StoreWriteError stack trace naming lib/todo-repository.js:65 and bin/todo.js:27, instead of `Error: could not save todo store: <reason>`. Reproduced identically on re-probe.

criteria.criterion: UC-CompleteTodo Steps 2-4 - index validated before TodoRepository.load(); E_MISSING_INDEX handling states 'no store access attempted'
criteria.evidence: cmdDone calls repo.load() at bin/todo.js:53 before parseIndex at bin/todo.js:64, inverting spec step order. Probe: corrupted store `{{bad` + `node bin/todo.js done` -> `Error: todo store is corrupted (...)` instead of the spec's E_MISSING_INDEX; `done abc` likewise yields E_STORE_CORRUPTED instead of E_INVALID_INDEX. Reproduced on re-probe.

criteria.criterion: UC-RemoveTodo Steps 2-4 - index validated before TodoRepository.load(); E_MISSING_INDEX handling states 'no store access attempted'
criteria.evidence: cmdRm calls repo.load() at bin/todo.js:85 before parseIndex at bin/todo.js:96. Probe: corrupted store + `node bin/todo.js rm` and `rm abc` both print `Error: todo store is corrupted (...)` instead of E_MISSING_INDEX / E_INVALID_INDEX. Reproduced on re-probe.

criteria.criterion: ux-behavior#Error-Catalog E_MISSING_INDEX user message is `Error: missing index`
criteria.evidence: MissingIndexError message is 'index is required' at lib/parse-index.js:5, rendered as `Error: ${err.code} - ${err.message}` by bin/todo.js:66. Probe: 1-item store + `node bin/todo.js done` -> `Error: E_MISSING_INDEX - index is required`, not `Error: missing index`. Reproduced on re-probe.

criteria.criterion: ux-behavior#Error-Catalog E_INVALID_INDEX user message is `Error: "<n>" is not a valid index`
criteria.evidence: InvalidIndexError message is `invalid index: "<raw>"` at lib/parse-index.js:13. Probe: `node bin/todo.js done zz` -> `Error: E_INVALID_INDEX - invalid index: "zz"`, not `Error: "zz" is not a valid index`. Reproduced on re-probe.

criteria.criterion: ux-behavior#Error-Catalog E_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE user message is `Error: no todo at index <n>`
criteria.evidence: IndexOutOfRangeError message is `index <n> out of range (1-<len>)` at lib/parse-index.js:21. Probe: 1-item store + `node bin/todo.js done 7` -> `Error: E_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE - index 7 out of range (1-1)`, not `Error: no todo at index 7`. Reproduced on re-probe.

assumptions: The order carried no run_cmd. This is a non-UI CLI with a single entry point (package.json bin -> ./bin/todo.js), so every probe invoked `node bin/todo.js <args>` directly rather than escalating.

Store isolation was achieved by setting HOME per invocation, since lib/todo-repository.js:32 resolves the store via os.homedir(); Node honours $HOME on this platform (verified: HOME=/tmp/ev1 node -e "os.homedir()" -> /tmp/ev1).

The order listed no t0_artifacts, but the six per-scope verdicts exist on disk and their sha256 values were recomputed by this evaluator and matched t0/trials.jsonl exactly; they are cited on that basis.
deviations: Spec defect surfaced, not silently passed: the success-message format is self-contradictory across committed docs. ux-behavior#done-command specifies `Done: N) <text>` (unquoted) while UC-CompleteTodo's System Flow specifies `Done: "2) buy milk"` (quoted); same split for rm. The build emits the quoted UC form. Graded against the UC as the designated source of truth, so no FAIL was recorded - but the two documents must be reconciled or this stays an arbitrary judgement call.

Tolerance recorded: E_MISSING_TEXT prints `Error: missing todo text (E_MISSING_TEXT)` where the catalog says `Error: missing todo text`. Counted PASS as a superset containing the required sentence; if BUG-03 is fixed by dropping code prefixes, align this for symmetry.

An early probe ran before HOME isolation was confirmed and wrote ~/.todo.json in the real home directory. It was detected immediately, contained only probe data, and was deleted; all subsequent probes set HOME inline per invocation.
